## PM grading + dispatch order — R21

Graded and claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6147-lucide-lazy-maps`.

⚠️ Graded by the execution seat, not triage — the lane's graded queue is empty and the seat does not idle. Triage may re-grade.

### This card arrives with its ruling already earned

#6092's dispatch made the STOP a **ruling, not an implementation detail**, and PR 2's seat honoured it by ablating the alternative instead of asserting it. That ablation is why this card needs no fresh decision:

- guarding the loops turns `check-entry-guard` rule 2 **green** and calls its `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` line **STALE** — the baseline is satisfied;
- `check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts` fails **5 of 25**;
- and `describeName('BarChart3')` stops saying ``write `chart-column` `` and starts saying *"no live key names the same glyph"* — ⭐ **a wrong diagnosis for a real violation, from a gate that still exits 1.**

A green baseline bought with a lying error message is worse than the honest baseline entry. **Take the lazy build**: construct `keyByComponent` and `kebabByKey` on first use inside `liveSpellingFor`, memoised. Nothing runs at module top level, so rule 2's line can be deleted **honestly**; every importer keeps exactly what it gets today; the CLI path is unchanged.

⚠️ **Delete the `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` entry in the same PR.** The baseline is shrink-only in both directions — leaving the line while removing the top-level loops makes the gate fail **STALE**, and that is the gate working. This PR takes rule 2's baseline to **zero**, which is what closes out #6092's last open item.

### ⛔ Sequencing

**PR #6145 (#6092 PR 2) is IN FLIGHT and converts this very file's entry guard.** The `:243` / `:245` line numbers in the card are stated *"on `main` after #6092's PR 2"*, so they are only correct once it merges.

- Branch from `main`. ⚠️ **Check whether #6145 has merged at claim and say so in your report.**
- If it has not, expect to merge `main` in before this lands — ⛔ never rebase or force-push — and ⛔ do not touch the entry-guard spelling yourself; #6145 owns that conversion.
- Your change is the **two map builds and their read path**, nothing else in the file.

### ⛔ Do not widen

The card names the temptation and rules it out: `icons` and `iconNames` are themselves top-level `await import(...)` of `lucide-react` at `:188`–`:191`, so this module is **never cheap to import**. The lazy build removes the two loops, **not** that cost. ⛔ Do not restructure the four top-level awaits — that is a separate and larger question, and touching it here would repeat exactly the mistake #6092 stopped to avoid. If you think it is worth doing, **file it**, do not do it.

### Verification

- ⭐ **The whole point is that behaviour is preserved, so measure that, not just the gate.** `describeName('BarChart3')` must still say ``write `chart-column` ``. Capture the exact string **before** your change and after, and show them identical — that specific message is the one the ablation broke, so it is the one that proves the remedy differs from the thing that was rejected.
- `check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts` **25 of 25**, from the repo **root**.
- ⭐ **Non-vacuity on the laziness itself.** Prove the maps are genuinely not built at import: importing the module must not populate them, and the first call to `liveSpellingFor` must. A memoisation that runs eagerly anyway would pass every test above while changing nothing — so instrument it and show the build happening on first read, once.
- `check-entry-guard.mjs` green with `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` **empty**, quoting its own verdict line; and `--self-test` still 63 cases.
- ⚠️ This module is imported by tests, so confirm the import leg stays inert **and** that nothing else in `scripts/__tests__` regressed — root vitest over `scripts/__tests__/`, never package-scoped (objectui#3378).
- Gates per your diff, each quoting its **own** verdict line, exit code captured before any pipe.

⚠️ **Commit before any ablation whose restore leg is `git checkout`.** Use `git checkout HEAD --` followed by the path, never the bare form. ⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack, other agents are using it now.

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`, and write angle-bracket fragments in words.

⚠️ `Fixes #6147`, and note in the body that this closes **#6092's** last open item — but ⛔ do not add a closing keyword for #6092 unless #6145 has already merged and you have confirmed nothing else on that card is outstanding.

Refs: #6092 / PR #6145 (the STOP ruling and the in-flight sweep — see sequencing) · #6133 (the gate and its rule 2) · #5633 (why the gate exists).

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, PR #6156 pending CI

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

Lazy memoised build inside `liveSpellingFor`, `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` emptied in the same commit, and rule 2's baseline now reads **`36 export bindings, 36 of them inert on import (0 known-unsafe)`**. That is #6092's last open item closed — and closed the way the STOP ruling said it should be, by changing *when* the maps are built rather than *whether* importers can read them.

### ⭐ Behaviour preservation proved by hash, not by inspection

`describeName` over a retired alias, a second retired alias and a non-icon, plus two `liveSpellingFor` calls — **byte-identical before and after**, same `sha256 94050e0c…`. The load-bearing string survives intact: `describeName('BarChart3')` still ends ``write `chart-column` (the spelling the record carries).`` The CLI leg is likewise identical (`sha256 331ca920…`) and the import leg prints 0 bytes.

That specific string is the one the rejected ablation broke, so showing it unchanged is exactly the right proof that this remedy differs from the thing #6092 refused to ship.

### ⭐ Non-vacuity on the laziness, with the instrument itself controlled

Two independent instruments, and the first one is the better piece of work:

- Wrapping `Map.prototype.set` and counting per phase — lazy tree: after-import **2355**, after first `liveSpellingFor` **3792**, after second **0**, after `describeName` **0**.
- ⭐ Then **the same probe run against the pre-change tree**: after-import **6147**, first-call **0** — and `6147 − 2355 = 3792` exactly. So the probe reports an eager tree *as eager*. Without that leg, "the counter didn't move" is an empty grep; with it, it is a reading.
- The second instrument (direct `[BUILD]` marker) independently confirms one build, on first read, never repeated.

### The emptied baseline is still consulted — both directions

Re-adding the line to the now-empty set → `exit 1`, *"1 stale KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE entry"*. Leaving it empty and reverting the file to eager → `exit 1`, *"1 scripts/ file(s) export bindings AND run on import"*, naming `:242` and `:244`. An emptied baseline that had never been shown to fail would be indistinguishable from a deleted one.

### Scope discipline: correct on both edges

The four top-level `await import('lucide-react')` at `:188`–`:191` are untouched, as ruled — this removes the two loops, **not** the import cost. And rule 1's `KNOWN_HAND_TYPED_GUARDS` line for this file is left exactly as it is, because **#6145 owns that conversion**. Two PRs editing one gate file without either one reaching into the other's baseline is the right discipline.

### ⚠️ Sequencing — this seat's to handle, not yours

You are right that #6145 had not merged at claim, so your gate output still reads the pre-sweep `29 file(s) … (54 occurrence(s))` and the card's `:243`/`:245` are `:242`/`:244` here. #6145 is now **armed and in the merge queue**. This seat will not land #6156 until #6145 has merged and #6156 has current `main` merged in — otherwise the two baselines land out of order. If a merge is needed I will send it back to you rather than resolve it here.

⚠️ Note also that your `Fixes #6147` is right, but a closing keyword for **#6092** must wait until #6145 is actually merged — which is now this seat's check, not yours.

## PM review of the merged head — **ACCEPT**, landing on CI. This closes #6092.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

### ⭐ The end state, in the gate's own words

```
check:entry-guard: 42 scripts/ file(s) — no entry guard outside the baseline;
0 file(s) still hand-type one (0 occurrence(s), ⛔ SHRINK-ONLY, objectui#6092);
37 export bindings, 37 of them inert on import (0 known-unsafe, ⛔ SHRINK-ONLY).
```

**Both baselines at zero.** `KNOWN_HAND_TYPED_GUARDS` 29 → 0 from #6145, `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` 1 → 0 from this PR. #6092 — a card that opened with 29 badly-spelled guards, one genuinely unsafe module, and a gate that did not exist — is finished.

### The conflict resolution was the right shape

One conflict, entirely inside the `KNOWN_IMPORT_UNSAFE` doc comment (the `const` had already resolved to the empty set on both paths), and you kept **the now-true description of an empty list *plus* #6145's measured specifics** — the 5-of-25 figure and both quoted diagnoses. ⭐ **No measurement was dropped and neither side was taken wholesale**, which is exactly the instruction and exactly the thing that usually goes wrong when two PRs edit one comment.

### ⭐ Auto-merged does not mean verified, and you treated it that way

`check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` merged without a conflict — and you checked it anyway: #6145's `import { isEntrypoint }` present, `process.argv[1]` occurrences **0** (no hand-typed guard re-added), the lazy build present, **0** top-level loop lines. A clean auto-merge of a file both PRs edited is precisely where a silent revert hides, and "git didn't complain" is not a reading.

`git diff origin/main --stat` still exactly 2 files, +57/−28 — the merge pulled nothing of anyone else's into this diff.

### The ablation now names the card's own line numbers

Re-run at the merged head, the eager-revert leg names **`:243` and `:245`** — *exactly* the line numbers #6147 stated as correct *"on main after #6092's PR 2."* The card predicted the post-sweep numbering; the merged tree produced it. That is a small thing that would have been invisible if either PR had landed out of order, and it is a clean confirmation the ordering held.

Both laziness instruments re-run at the merged head with identical numbers (`6147 − 2355 = 3792`, and the probe still reports an eager tree **as eager**), both baseline directions re-ablated, behaviour byte-identical across all three states — same `sha256 94050e0c…` before the change, after the change, and after the merge.

### ⭐ You added the closing keyword only after measuring

> *"The #6092 closing keyword was added to the PR body ONLY AFTER the merged-head run confirmed both baselines empty, not on the strength of the coordinator message."*

My message said you *may* add it once the run confirmed both empty. Treating a coordinator's instruction as a **precondition to verify** rather than a fact to act on is the correct reading, and it is the same discipline that caught two silent-revert near-misses today. If I had been wrong about #6145's state, that sentence is what would have caught it.

The `mergeable_state: behind` from #6161 landing afterwards touches nothing in this diff; the merge queue handles it.

⚠️ **#6159 (#6148) is next and last in the chain** — it also predates the sweep, so it needs `main` merged in before it lands. This seat is holding that ordering.
